quiz.title: Chapter 14 Quiz: Practice-Specific Research
quiz.intro: Ten questions on the three parameters that change with the practice context, and the closure criterion for each.

items.q: According to the chapter, what changes from one practice context to the next?
options: The five steps of the cycle
The parameters the cycle runs with: default question type, first source, and closure criterion
The need for a Research Log
items.why: The cycle is context-neutral; only the parameters move (Practice-Specific Research and the Research Cycle).

items.q: Litigation research runs heavily on which question type?
options: Application: how have the controlling cases applied the rule to facts like these?
items.why: Transactional work runs on focusing questions about requirements and risks; regulatory work spans all four (Practice-Specific Research and the Research Cycle).

items.q: The first source for transactional research is usually:
items.why: Litigation starts in case law; regulatory work in the CFR and agency guidance (Practice-Specific Research and the Research Cycle).

items.q: Which closure criterion belongs to litigation?
options: All applicable requirements and risks identified
Controlling authority for each issue; adverse authority identified and addressed; procedural requirements confirmed; authorities updated
items.why: Closing out by the wrong criterion is a close relative of importing one context’s habits into another (Litigation Research; Common Pitfalls).

items.q: SEC EDGAR is named as essential for:
options: Federal securities research: public company filings, prospectuses, and precedent transaction documents

items.q: The meta-question the chapter wants you to ask in any unfamiliar context is:
options: Which database has the best interface?
In this context, what is my default question type, where do I start, and what will tell me I’m done?
How many cases should I cite?
items.why: A lawyer who has internalized the cycle can walk into an unfamiliar area and ask it immediately (Practice-Specific Research and the Research Cycle).

items.q: In regulatory and compliance research, closure also requires:
options: Checking pending rulemaking for upcoming changes and reviewing recent enforcement actions
items.why: Map every obligation, consult guidance, review enforcement priorities (Regulatory and Compliance Research).

items.q: The Research Log changes function across contexts. In transactional practice it:
options: Documents the authority behind each argument
items.why: In litigation it documents authority; in regulatory practice it maps obligations (Practice-Specific Research and the Research Cycle).

items.q: Why does the chapter say a new lawyer’s reflex for a familiar source type ripens into the single-source trap in a new practice area?
options: Because the authority types that govern the new context are exactly the ones old habits never taught you to open
Because case law is always wrong in transactions
items.why: See Chapter 8 for the trap’s two forms (Common Pitfalls).

items.q: The Kiss Pharm excerpt shows a court:
options: Chastising counsel whose motion ignored a settled body of case law
items.why: In litigation, the arguments you make must be supported by judicial authority (Litigation Research).
